The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim. A fantasy role-playing game developed by Bethesda Game Studios, released in 2011 for PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, and PC. Set in the Nordic province of Skyrim, you explore dragon-filled landscapes, join factions, craft gear, and pursue a main quest to defeat the world-ending dragon Alduin. Its emphasis on player agency, modding community, and exploration made it one of gaming's most enduring titles. The open world is divided into nine holds, each with towns, dungeons, and wilderness. You traverse freely from the start, though underleveled areas will punish early exploration. The protagonist is Dragonborn—able to absorb dragon souls and use Thu'um, which is the dragon shout, unlocking powerful abilities tied to the narrative of ancient dragon worship. Four joinable factions shape your playstyle: the Thieves Guild for stealth and larceny, the Dark Brotherhood for assassination, the College of Winterhold for magic, and the Stormcloaks versus Imperial Legion for a civil war. Crafting is central to progression—alchemy, smithing, and enchanting let you loot raw materials and craft or improve weapons, armor, and potions to customize your build. Dragon encounters are unpredictable and dramatic, populating Skyrim as part of the main plot and serving as both main-quest markers and random open-world threats. The modding community has sustained the game's popularity for over a decade, with mods ranging from visual overhauls to gameplay mechanics to total conversion projects. The game was released on Nintendo Switch in 2017, PlayStation VR in 2020, and re-released on PC in 2021 as Anniversary Edition, a testament to its staying power.
